name: personality
description: Traits, ideals, quirks, bonds, and flaws

entries.value: Cheerfully fatalistic; treats every disaster as confirmation of a prediction nobody remembers hearing.
Painfully honest but highly skilled at changing the subject before revealing anything personal.
Suspicious of all magic except one obviously fraudulent superstition followed with complete devotion.
Grandly theatrical in public, quiet and observant in private, and terrified of being considered ordinary.
Collects favors instead of money and remembers every promise with unsettling precision.
Protective of underdogs, openly rude to authority, and unable to resist proving a bully wrong.
Polite to enemies and brutally critical of friends because respect is expressed through honesty.
Believes every problem has a practical solution, even when facing ghosts, prophecy, or divine judgment.
Compulsively adopts stray animals and assigns each one a military rank.
Treats coincidences as sacred messages and constantly rearranges plans to follow them.
Generous with possessions but jealous of attention, especially when a rival tells a better story.
Never raises their voice; the calmer they sound, the angrier and more dangerous they are.
Obsessed with etiquette from a culture they only understand through an inaccurate old book.
Claims to fear nothing except geese, and refuses to explain the very specific reason.
Loyal to any agreement's exact wording while exploiting every loophole without guilt.
Eager to forgive personal insults but incapable of overlooking harm done to a stranger.
Constantly invents impressive former careers; a surprising number later prove true.
Treats combat like a puzzle and social interaction like an unavoidable natural disaster.
Wants to be feared but automatically comforts anyone who looks upset.
Keeps meticulous journals yet replaces every person's name with an increasingly confusing nickname.
Sees wealth as a burden and spends it recklessly on memorable experiences and ridiculous gifts.
Deeply religious but argues with their deity as if speaking to an irritating family member.
Cannot admit ignorance and improvises explanations that often become accidental local legends.
Values freedom above safety but becomes controlling whenever companions are genuinely endangered.
Apologizes to every defeated enemy and becomes offended if the apology is rejected.
Speaks in proverbs, most of which are invented on the spot and only loosely relevant.
Appears cynical and mercenary but secretly sends most earnings to rebuild a ruined hometown.
Always assumes the best of monsters and the worst of institutions.
Keeps trophies from failures rather than victories and can recount every lesson attached to them.
Desperate to leave a heroic legacy, yet freezes whenever someone recognizes them in public.
Welcoming and attentive, puts newcomers at ease but becomes involved in their problems too quickly.
Ambitious, measures every relationship by what it may help them accomplish.
Playful and funny, defuses tense situations with humor even when the moment is inappropriate.
Arrogant, treats competence as self-evident and every correction as a personal attack.
A passionate artist who seeks beauty even in dangerous places and neglects practical needs.
Authoritarian, naturally organizes others but struggles when a decision escapes their control.
Miserly, hoards money, information, and favors until spending them becomes absolutely necessary.
Talkative, readily shares stories and rumors but sometimes reveals protected information.
A smooth talker who makes proposals attractive without directly lying about their flaws.
Jaded, greets wonders and disasters with equal weariness while carefully watching everyone else.
Gruff but loyal, expresses affection through practical deeds rather than kind words.
Capricious, abruptly changes priorities and expects close companions to follow without explanation.
Charismatic, naturally draws attention but feels responsible for everyone who follows.
Wildly unpredictable, follows a private logic that others struggle to understand in the moment.
Hot-tempered, reacts sharply to provocation and regrets the damage after calming down.
Courageous, moves through fear and downplays danger to reassure others.
Courteous even toward enemies and immediately notices every breach of etiquette.
Creative, improvises unexpected solutions but quickly loses interest in implementing them.
Cultured, relates every situation to scholarship and forgets that others may not share the reference.
Curious, asks the question everyone avoids and willingly touches what should remain intact.
Cynical about institutions, yet quietly helps people who prove sincere.
Disorganized, effortlessly finds personal belongings in chaos nobody else understands.
Depressed and deeply discouraged, withdraws and struggles to find interest or energy for action.
Devoted, places a person or cause before comfort and misses when that loyalty is exploited.
Reserved, listens more than speaks and dislikes public recognition.
Absent-minded, notices unusual details while forgetting obvious obligations.
Selfish about personal safety but surprisingly generous toward the few considered family.
Emotional, openly shows joy, fear, and anger, making intentions easy to read.
Energetic, turns every delay into activity and sometimes exhausts companions.
Enigmatic, answers with images and half-truths because being understood feels more dangerous than being judged.
Ingeniously lazy, works hard to invent ways around repetitive labor.
Proud, welcomes challenges but refuses help that might imply inadequacy.
A party-lover who quickly starts celebrations and accepts every rough morning as the price of a good story.
Devious, bends rules rather than openly breaking them and always keeps an escape route.
Blunt, speaks plainly and sometimes confuses honesty with tactlessness.
Outwardly cold, controls reactions to protect a much deeper attachment.
Accident-prone in ordinary moments but surprisingly effective in a real crisis.
Haughty, judges people by bearing and reputation until forced to revise the opinion.
Foolish, repeatedly misreads situations and confidently commits to poor decisions.
Impatient and impulsive, prefers an immediate bad decision to waiting without information.
Insolent, challenges authority by reflex but respects people who justify decisions clearly.
Ironic, uses sarcasm for distance and becomes direct when someone is truly endangered.
Jealous, constantly compares their place with others while feeling ashamed of needing recognition.
Nervous, anticipates every possible failure and is often better prepared than the optimists.
Fair-minded, applies the same principles to allies and enemies even at personal cost.
Logical, seeks verifiable causes and treats magic as an underdocumented problem.
Clumsy, lacks physical ease but quickly recognizes people who feel awkward or excluded.
Compulsively orderly, relies on precise rituals of control that become fragile under pressure.
Mysterious, protects the past with vague answers but never lies about present danger.
Modest, minimizes achievements and gives away credit until someone claims the work.
A compulsive fabulist who embellishes personal history and becomes trapped in invented stories.
Naive, trusts first but remembers every betrayal for a long time.
Optimistic, seeks opportunity in every crisis and refuses to let fatalism decide.
Pacifist, always seeks a nonviolent solution but prepares carefully in case it fails.
Passionate, gives everything to one project and forgets the world while enthusiasm lasts.
Patient, lets others reveal themselves and acts only at the decisive moment.
Sexually inappropriate, frequently turns exchanges toward sexual concerns or innuendo and crosses social boundaries.
Fearful but cautious, avoids needless risk and often spots danger before bolder heroes.
Protective, takes responsibility for vulnerable people and struggles when unable to control every risk.
Resentful, remembers offenses exactly but may abandon revenge after sincere amends.
Rebellious, rejects rules based only on tradition and demands that authority prove legitimacy.
A dreamer who imagines other lives and worlds, sometimes missing what happens nearby.
Wise, prefers the right question to an immediate answer and admits ignorance.
Schizophrenic, currently experiences disorganized or altered reality without that defining intentions or dangerousness.
Sensitive, quickly reads a group’s emotions but readily absorbs its tensions.
Serious, treats every commitment rigorously and does not always understand others’ need for levity.
Helpful, offers assistance before being asked and often hides personal exhaustion.
Solitary, fiercely protects independence while secretly hoping to be invited to stay.
Submissive, yields to confident authority and prefers following a decision to risking confrontation.
Touchy, hears ordinary criticism as a global judgment but fiercely defends unfairly criticized people.
Stubborn, holds decisions past reason but remains an exceptionally constant ally.
Shy, avoids attention while carefully preparing what to say if invited to speak.
A cheater who sees rules as negotiable obstacles and respects opponents who expose the method.
Boastful, exaggerates exploits but nearly always accepts the challenge needed to prove them.
Violent, turns to force too quickly and seeks moral justification afterward.
A bon vivant who values food, company, and comfort without abandoning friends when the party ends.
